```{r Step 0: Pull in ANES Data, include=TRUE}
anes_panel <- read_dta(here("00_rawdata", "ANES_Data", "anes_timeseries_cdf_stata_20260205.dta"))
```

```{r Step 1: Cleaning Up the Dataset, include=TRUE}
# Check the variables
anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  rename(year = VCF0004, trust_gov_index = VCF0656, trust_gov = VCF0604, econ_views = VCF0870, stock_owns = VCF9224, social_class = VCF0149, person_finances = VCF0880, person_finances_scale = VCF0880a, personal_finances_next = VCF0881, age = VCF0101, age_group = VCF0102, gender = VCF0104, race = VCF0105a, educ = VCF0110, income_group = VCF0114, emp_status = VCF0116, homeowner = VCF0146, marital_stat = VCF0147, partisan_id = VCF0301, partisan_strength = VCF0305, pol_interest = VCF0310, union_mem = VCF0127)


#Initial Diagnostics
anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    personal_finances_change = case_when(
      as.numeric(person_finances_scale) %in% 1:5 ~ as.numeric(person_finances_scale),
      as.numeric(person_finances_scale) %in% c(8, 9) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    personal_finances_scale_factor = factor(
      personal_finances_change,
      levels = 1:5,
      labels = c(
        "Much better",
        "Somewhat better",
        "Same",
        "Somewhat worse",
        "Much worse"
      )
    )
  )

anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    personal_finances_scale_clean = case_when(
      as.numeric(person_finances_scale) %in% 1:5 ~
        as.numeric(person_finances_scale),
      as.numeric(person_finances_scale) %in% c(8, 9) ~
        NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    personal_finance_direction = case_when(
      personal_finances_scale_clean %in% c(1, 2) ~ "Better",
      personal_finances_scale_clean == 3 ~ "Same",
      personal_finances_scale_clean %in% c(4, 5) ~ "Worse",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    personal_finance_direction = factor(
      personal_finance_direction,
      levels = c("Better", "Same", "Worse")
    )
  )
#Recoding Variables (Brought Over from Part 1)
anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    trust_gov_index = na_if(trust_gov_index, 999)
  )

#Same Thing for Economic Views
anes_panel %>%
  filter(year >= 2000, year <= 2024) %>%
  count(econ_views, sort = TRUE)

#Recode Data to Only show valid entries
anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    trust_gov_index = na_if(trust_gov_index, 999),
    econ_views = case_when(
      econ_views %in% c(1, 3, 5) ~ econ_views,
      econ_views %in% c(8, 9) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    # Trust
    trust_gov_index = if_else(
      trust_gov_index == 999,
      NA_real_,
      as.numeric(trust_gov_index)
    ),

    # Economic views
    econ_views = case_when(
      as.numeric(econ_views) %in% c(1, 3, 5) ~ as.numeric(econ_views),
      as.numeric(econ_views) %in% c(8, 9) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # Stock ownership
    stock_owns = case_when(
      as.numeric(stock_owns) == 1 ~ 1,
      as.numeric(stock_owns) == 2 ~ 0,
      as.numeric(stock_owns) %in% c(-8, -9) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # Homeownership
    homeowner = case_when(
      as.numeric(homeowner) == 1 ~ 1,
      as.numeric(homeowner) == 2 ~ 0,
      as.numeric(homeowner) %in% c(8, 9) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # Income percentile group
    income_group = as.numeric(income_group)
  )

anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    econ_views_factor = factor(
      econ_views,
      levels = c(1, 3, 5),
      labels = c(
        "Get better",
        "Stay about the same",
        "Get worse"
      )
    ),

    income_group_factor = factor(
      income_group,
      levels = 1:5,
      labels = c(
        "0–16th percentile",
        "17–33rd percentile",
        "34–67th percentile",
        "68–95th percentile",
        "96–100th percentile"
      )
    )
  )

#Adding in new variable - external efficacy index
anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  rename(
    efficacy_index = VCF0648
  )

summary(anes_panel$efficacy_index)

table(
  anes_panel$efficacy_index,
  useNA = "ifany"
)

anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    efficacy_index = case_when(
      as.numeric(efficacy_index) %in% 1:100 ~ as.numeric(efficacy_index),
      as.numeric(efficacy_index) >100 ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  ) 

anes_panel %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(efficacy_index)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n > 0)

anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  rename(
    government_care = VCF0609
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    government_care = case_when(
      as.numeric(government_care) %in% 1:3 ~ as.numeric(government_care),
      as.numeric(government_care) == 9 ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    government_care_factor = factor(
      government_care,
      levels = 1:3,
      labels = c(
        "Agree",
        "Disagree",
        "Neither"
      )
    )
  )

anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  rename(
    government_say = VCF0613
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    government_say = case_when(
      as.numeric(government_say) %in% 1:3 ~ as.numeric(government_say),
      as.numeric(government_say) == 9 ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    government_say_factor = factor(
      government_say,
      levels = 1:3,
      labels = c(
        "Agree",
        "Disagree",
        "Neither"
      )
    )
  )

table(
  anes_panel$government_say,
  useNA = "ifany"
)

#Turn Dataset into Survey Object
anes_svy <- anes_panel %>%
  filter(year >= 2000) %>%
  as_survey_design(
    ids = 1,
    weights = VCF0009z
  ) 

anes_svy

anes_panel <- anes_panel %>%
  mutate(
    government_services = case_when(
      as.numeric(VCF0839) %in% 1:7 ~ as.numeric(VCF0839),
      as.numeric(VCF0839) == 9 ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    
    government_jobs = case_when(
      as.numeric(VCF0809) %in% 1:7 ~ as.numeric(VCF0809),
      as.numeric(VCF0809) == 9 ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

services_income <- anes_panel %>%
  filter(
    year >= 2000,
    year <= 2024,
    !is.na(government_services),
    !is.na(income_group),
    !is.na(VCF0009z)
  ) %>%
  group_by(year, income_group) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_services = weighted.mean(
      government_services,
      w = VCF0009z,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

services_income

services_income <- services_income %>%
  mutate(
    income_group_factor = factor(
      income_group,
      levels = 1:5,
      labels = c(
        "0–16th percentile",
        "17–33rd percentile",
        "34–67th percentile",
        "68–95th percentile",
        "96–100th percentile"
      )
    )
  )

ggplot(
  services_income,
  aes(
    x = income_group_factor,
    y = mean_services,
    group = 1
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(1, 7),
    breaks = 1:7
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Income group",
    y = "Mean government-services spending scale",
    title = "Preferences for government services by income"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1)
  )

services_income_stock_plot <- services_income_stock %>%

#Income Gradient Additional Descriptive Measure
services_income_stock %>%
  group_by(year, stock_owns_factor) %>%
  summarise(
    income_gradient =
      mean_services[income_group == 5] -
      mean_services[income_group == 1],
    .groups = "drop"
  )

jobs_income_stock %>%
  group_by(year, stock_owns_factor) %>%
  summarise(
    income_gradient =
      mean_jobs[income_group == 5] -
      mean_jobs[income_group == 1],
    .groups = "drop"

#A substantial income gradient in economic policy preferences through much of the 2000–2020 period that largely collapses by 2024, with the magnitude and occasionally the direction of that gradient varying considerably by stock ownership.
```

```{r Step 2: Initial Modeling for Government Services Measure, include=TRUE}
services_income_time <- anes_panel %>%
  filter(
    year >= 2000,
    year <= 2024,
    !is.na(government_services),
    !is.na(income_group_factor),
    !is.na(VCF0009z)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year_factor = factor(year)
  )

design_services_income_time <- survey::svydesign(
  ids = ~1,
  weights = ~VCF0009z,
  data = services_income_time
)

model_services_income_time <- survey::svyglm(
  government_services ~
    income_group_factor * year_factor,
  design = design_services_income_time
)

summary(model_services_income_time)

regTermTest(
  model_services_income_time,
  ~ income_group_factor:year_factor
)
#The association between income and preferences regarding government provision of services varies significantly across survey years, with the pronounced income gradient evident in earlier waves substantially attenuated by 2024.

services_income_stock_time <- anes_panel %>%
  filter(
    year >= 2000,
    year <= 2024,
    !is.na(government_services),
    !is.na(income_group_factor),
    !is.na(stock_owns),
    !is.na(VCF0009z)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year_factor = factor(year)
  )

design_services_income_stock_time <- survey::svydesign(
  ids = ~1,
  weights = ~VCF0009z,
  data = services_income_stock_time
)

model_services_income_stock_time <- survey::svyglm(
  government_services ~
    income_group_factor *
    stock_owns *
    year_factor,
  design = design_services_income_stock_time
)

summary(model_services_income_stock_time)

regTermTest(
  model_services_income_stock_time,
  ~ income_group_factor:stock_owns:year_factor
)
#So there is evidence that the income × stock-ownership relationship in government-services preferences varies across survey years. Put differently, the way income is associated with support for government services/spending is not stable across time for stock owners versus non-stock owners


#Predicted Probabilities
services_predictions <- emmeans::emmeans(
  model_services_income_stock_time,
  ~ income_group_factor * stock_owns | year_factor,
  at = list(
    year_factor = c("2000", "2012", "2020", "2024")
  )
)

services_predictions

services_predictions_df <- as.data.frame(services_predictions) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(income_group_factor),
    !is.na(stock_owns),
    !is.na(year_factor)
  )

services_predictions_df
#So in 2024, stock ownership is associated with lower support for government services across the income distribution, not simply at the very top. By 2024 the income gradient has largely disappeared in both ownership groups.
```

```{r Step 3: Initial Modeling for Government Jobs Measure, include=TRUE}
jobs_income_time <- anes_panel %>%
  filter(
    year >= 2000,
    year <= 2024,
    !is.na(government_jobs),
    !is.na(income_group_factor),
    !is.na(VCF0009z)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year_factor = factor(year)
  )

design_jobs_income_time <- survey::svydesign(
  ids = ~1,
  weights = ~VCF0009z,
  data = jobs_income_time
)

model_jobs_income_time <- survey::svyglm(
  government_jobs ~
    income_group_factor * year_factor,
  design = design_jobs_income_time
)

summary(model_jobs_income_time)


regTermTest(
  model_jobs_income_time,
  ~ income_group_factor:year_factor
)

jobs_predictions <- emmeans::emmeans(
  model_jobs_income_time,
  ~ income_group_factor | year_factor,
  at = list(
    year_factor = c("2000", "2012", "2020", "2024")
  )
)

jobs_predictions_df <- as.data.frame(jobs_predictions) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(income_group_factor),
    !is.na(year_factor)
  )

jobs_predictions_df
#There is therefore a meaningful contrast with your government-services outcome. For services, the income gradient was strongly negative in 2000 and essentially disappeared by 2024. For jobs/government responsibility, the gradient is generally positive in the earlier period and also becomes much weaker by 2024. income-based differentiation in economic-policy attitudes are becoming substantially less pronounced by 2024


#Three-Way Test
jobs_income_stock_time <- anes_panel %>%
  filter(
    year >= 2000,
    year <= 2024,
    !is.na(government_jobs),
    !is.na(income_group_factor),
    !is.na(stock_owns),
    !is.na(VCF0009z)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year_factor = factor(year)
  )

design_jobs_income_stock_time <- survey::svydesign(
  ids = ~1,
  weights = ~VCF0009z,
  data = jobs_income_stock_time
)

model_jobs_income_stock_time <- survey::svyglm(
  government_jobs ~
    income_group_factor *
    stock_owns *
    year_factor,
  design = design_jobs_income_stock_time
)

regTermTest(
  model_jobs_income_stock_time,
  ~ income_group_factor:stock_owns:year_factor
)

jobs_predictions <- emmeans::emmeans(
  model_jobs_income_stock_time,
  ~ income_group_factor * stock_owns | year_factor,
  at = list(
    year_factor = c("2000", "2012", "2020", "2024")
  )
)

jobs_predictions_df <- as.data.frame(jobs_predictions) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(income_group_factor),
    !is.na(year_factor)
  )

jobs_predictions_df
#The association between income and preferences over government responsibility for economic security varies substantially by asset ownership and historical period, with the income gradient becoming very weak within both asset groups by 2024. 2024 doesn't look like a simple substitution of stock ownership for income. Stock owners are substantially more supportive of individual responsibility than non-stock owners in 2024 across virtually every income category, but within each group, income itself has almost no gradient.

jobs_stock_comparisons <- emmeans::emmeans(
  model_jobs_income_stock_time,
  ~ stock_owns | income_group_factor * year_factor,
  at = list(
    year_factor = c("2000", "2012", "2020", "2024")
  )
)

pairs(jobs_stock_comparisons)
#From 2000 to 2024, the association between income and preferences over government responsibility for economic security varies by stock ownership and survey year. By 2024, income gradients are weak within both stock-owner and non-owner groups, while substantial stock-ownership differences remain across much of the income distribution. Income differentiation weakens, while asset-ownership differentiation persists

services_stock_comparisons <- emmeans::emmeans(
  model_services_income_stock_time,
  ~ stock_owns | income_group_factor * year_factor,
  at = list(
    year_factor = c("2000", "2012", "2020", "2024")
  )
)

pairs(services_stock_comparisons)
#The relationship between income and economic-policy preferences became substantially weaker within both stock-owner and non-stock-owner groups by 2024, while differences associated with stock ownership persisted across much of the income distribution.
```

```{r Step 4: Interacting Policy Preferences with Personal Financial Circumstances, include=TRUE}
# Personal finances × year: Government services

services_finance_time <- anes_panel %>%
  filter(
    year >= 2000,
    year <= 2024,
    !is.na(government_services),
    !is.na(personal_finances_scale_factor),
    !is.na(VCF0009z)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year_factor = factor(year)
  )

design_services_finance_time <- survey::svydesign(
  ids = ~1,
  weights = ~VCF0009z,
  data = services_finance_time
)

model_services_finance_time <- survey::svyglm(
  government_services ~
    personal_finances_scale_factor * year_factor,
  design = design_services_finance_time
)

summary(model_services_finance_time)

regTermTest(
  model_services_finance_time,
  ~ personal_finances_scale_factor:year_factor
)

services_finance_predictions <- emmeans::emmeans(
  model_services_finance_time,
  ~ personal_finances_scale_factor | year_factor,
  at = list(
    year_factor = c("2000", "2004", "2008", "2012",
                    "2016", "2020", "2024")
  )
)

services_finance_predictions

# Personal finances × stock ownership × year:
# Government services

services_finance_stock_time <- anes_panel %>%
  filter(
    year >= 2000,
    year <= 2024,
    !is.na(government_services),
    !is.na(personal_finances_scale_factor),
    !is.na(stock_owns),
    !is.na(VCF0009z)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year_factor = factor(year)
  )

design_services_finance_stock_time <- survey::svydesign(
  ids = ~1,
  weights = ~VCF0009z,
  data = services_finance_stock_time
)

model_services_finance_stock_time <- survey::svyglm(
  government_services ~
    personal_finances_scale_factor *
    stock_owns *
    year_factor,
  design = design_services_finance_stock_time
)

summary(model_services_finance_stock_time)

regTermTest(
  model_services_finance_stock_time,
  ~ personal_finances_scale_factor:
    stock_owns:
    year_factor
)

services_finance_stock_predictions <- emmeans::emmeans(
  model_services_finance_stock_time,
  ~ personal_finances_scale_factor * stock_owns | year_factor,
  at = list(
    year_factor = c(
      "2000", "2004", "2008",
      "2012", "2016", "2020", "2024"
    )
  )
)

services_finance_stock_predictions
#The relationship between subjective economic circumstances and policy preferences is itself historically contingent and differs according to asset ownership. The ownership-specific gradients actually reverse across periods. In particular, stock owners go from a very strong positive finance gradient in 2020 to a strong negative gradient in 2024.

services_finance_stock_2020_2024 <- emmeans::emmeans(
  model_services_finance_stock_time,
  ~ personal_finances_scale_factor * stock_owns | year_factor,
  at = list(
    year_factor = c("2020", "2024")
  )
)

services_finance_stock_2020_2024

services_finance_gradient_2020_2024 <- emmeans::contrast(
  services_finance_stock_2020_2024,
  method = list(
    "Much worse vs Much better" = c(-1, 0, 0, 0, 1)
  ),
  by = c("stock_owns", "year_factor")
)

summary(services_finance_gradient_2020_2024)

services_finance_DID <- emmeans::contrast(
  services_finance_gradient_2020_2024,
  method = list(
    "2020 vs 2024 change" = c(-1, 1)
  ),
  by = "stock_owns"
)

services_finance_DID

services_finance_DID_test <- emmeans::contrast(
  services_finance_DID,
  method = list(
    "Difference in change: stock vs non-stock" = c(-1, 1)
  ),
  by = NULL
)

summary(services_finance_DID_test)
```

```{r Step 5: Run this Model Sequence on Government Jobs Scale Measure, include=TRUE}
# Personal finances × year: Government jobs

jobs_finance_time <- anes_panel %>%
  filter(
    year >= 2000,
    year <= 2024,
    !is.na(government_jobs),
    !is.na(personal_finances_scale_factor),
    !is.na(VCF0009z)
  ) %>%
```

```{r Step 7: Plotting the Data, include=TRUE}
year_pairs <- list(
  "2000 → 2008" = c(2000, 2008),
  "2008 → 2012" = c(2008, 2012),
  "2012 → 2016" = c(2012, 2016),
  "2016 → 2020" = c(2016, 2020),
  "2020 → 2024" = c(2020, 2024)
)

calculate_gradient_changes <- function(gradient_object, outcome_name) {
  
  gradient_df <- summary(gradient_object) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    mutate(
      year = as.numeric(as.character(year_factor))
    )
  
  results <- lapply(names(year_pairs), function(pair_name) {
    
    years <- year_pairs[[pair_name]]
    year_start <- years[1]
    year_end <- years[2]
    
    start <- gradient_df %>%
      filter(year == year_start) %>%
      select(stock_owns, estimate_start = estimate, SE_start = SE)
    
    end <- gradient_df %>%
      filter(year == year_end) %>%
      select(stock_owns, estimate_end = estimate, SE_end = SE)
    
    start %>%
      inner_join(end, by = "stock_owns") %>%
      mutate(
        interval = pair_name,
        change = estimate_end - estimate_start,
        outcome = outcome_name
      )
  })
  
  bind_rows(results)
}

services_changes <- calculate_gradient_changes(
  services_gradient_all,
  "Government services"
)

jobs_changes <- calculate_gradient_changes(
  jobs_gradient_all,
  "Government jobs"
)

gradient_changes <- bind_rows(
  services_changes,
  jobs_changes
)

gradient_changes

jobs_interval_tests <- emmeans::contrast(

) %>%
```
